The structure is described in space group R-3 (number 148, Hall symbol -R 3), with the input cell given in a nonstandard rhombohedral-like setting having lattice parameters a = b = c = 7.79230124 Å and α = β = γ = 53.3173892° (with γ listed as 53.31739763°, a tiny rounding-level difference). The declared input composition is Hf₄Te₆, corresponding to 10 atoms in the input cell. Fractional coordinates are used, and the input and standard frames are related by q_standard = P q_input + s, where P has rows (2/3, -1/3, -1/3), (1/3, 1/3, -2/3), and (1/3, 1/3, 1/3), and the origin shift s is (0, 0, 0); thus the standard-frame description is obtained by applying that matrix to each input fractional coordinate without any translational offset.

In the standard frame, the hafnium sublattice is built from three independent orbits. One Hf orbit occupies Wyckoff site 3a with representative coordinate (0, 0, 0), giving three symmetry-equivalent Hf positions per conventional cell. A second, independent Hf orbit occupies Wyckoff site 6c with representative coordinate (0, 0, z) where z = 0.339866, giving six Hf positions related by the R-3 symmetry operations. A third Hf orbit occupies Wyckoff site 3b with representative coordinate (0, 0, 1/2), again giving three Hf positions. Together these orbits account for 12 Hf atoms in the conventional standard cell.

Tellurium occupies a single independent orbit on the general-position Wyckoff site 18f, with representative fractional coordinates (x, y, z) = (0.002841, 0.348972, 0.421258). This orbit has multiplicity 18, so the conventional standard cell contains 18 Te atoms generated from that one independent Te position. The overall conventional-cell contents implied by these multiplicities are therefore Hf₁₂Te₁₈, which is a 3× enlargement of the declared input-cell composition Hf₄Te₆, consistent with the rhombohedral R-centering description.

All coordinates are reported to six decimal places, and no precision corrections are required: the listed representative positions already define the independent geometry, with the remaining atoms generated by the R-3 symmetry operations in the standard frame and recoverable in the original input frame through the inverse of the stated transformation.
